title: Launch a public "Educators on Zedu" community workspace run on Zedu itself by Fri Dec 11
description: A space where bootcamp leads, lecturers and teachers who use Zedu share setups and ask questions, which shows the product working. Done = the workspace plan (channels, rules, moderation roles, a welcome flow), a launch post, an invite plan for the first 50 educators, a monthly Buzz "office hour" format, and how we keep it active and safe. Needs the team to confirm who moderates.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Seed the educator community with a moderated help-and-share loop before inviting fifty members
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Treat the workspace as a small educator support practice, with a launch gate: named human moderator and backup confirmed, rules approved, and real product workflows checked before invitations. Organise a compact welcome area, practical teaching questions, reusable cohort setups and an office-hour discussion; these are proposed channel purposes, not claimed existing templates or automations. Design a four-week host rota with one weekly question, one example setup and a closed-loop question status register, all maintained manually until capabilities are verified. Deliver one launch-readiness playbook containing the channel/rule plan, welcome and first-week seed posts, launch post, opt-in invitation plan for the first fifty educators, a monthly Buzz office-hour run sheet, and escalation/closure examples using fictional participants. Acceptance: every activity has an accountable host or an explicit approval dependency; the first week can run from the pack; three synthetic scenarios (unanswered question, inappropriate content, private learner data) each have a response and escalation route; no promise of always-on moderation or guaranteed response times. Measure unanswered-question age, distinct contributing educators and repeat participation with denominators; no invented engagement targets or results. Reuse existing workspace/guide materials and keep this one coherent deliverable. Unlike the pending generic implementation roadmap, this specifies the operating loop and launch gates that prevent an empty or unmoderated community. No workspace creation, invitations, public posts, personal data collection or live moderation without separate team approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before the public invite, define a practical moderator runbook for spam, harassment, privacy-sensitive posts, feature-support questions and heated disagreements. acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the first-50 invite and welcome emails, with a 50-name manifest and a human-send checklist
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The goal needs an invite plan for the first 50 educators and a welcome flow, but the two accepted workstreams cover seeding and moderation, not the invitation itself. Work: map the join path from invite to first post; write four short emails (invite, welcome with the rules and where to introduce yourself, a day-3 nudge, and a week-1 office-hour reminder), each with subject line, plain-text version and a one-line opt-out; define send timing and who sends; build a 50-name manifest template (name, role, institution, source, consent to be invited, date invited) and a no-send checklist. Do not contact anyone; the team sends after owner approval. Done: the copy, the flow diagram, the manifest template and the per-email measure (join rate, and share who post in week one).
